text: Preregistration should specify hypotheses, primary outcomes, analysis decisions, and stopping rules before data collection. Clearly distinguish confirmatory analyses from exploratory work.
A reproducible protocol documents a power analysis, a precision target, or a pilot-study rationale. Small pilot samples should limit claims of effectiveness.
Data management plans should specify collection, de-identification, access controls, retention, and a sharing approach that matches data sensitivity and consent.
Version-controlled analysis code, dependency documentation, and a release plan improve reproducibility and enable independent verification.
For randomized trials, protocols should document allocation procedures and assessor blinding, or give a clear justification when blinding is not feasible.
Protocols involving health or sensitive participant data should document the relevant ethics review, consent safeguards, and data access restrictions.
